records.title: Fix opt-in installation instructions
records.observation:
4 problems.
  1. The guide says the preference defaults to enabled. The code default is off. The commit that changed the default is titled Default TurboMCP user preference to off, so the code looks intentional and the guide looks out of date.
  2. The guide's section is about disabling TurboMCP for yourself. With an off default, most users first need to turn it on.
  3. The install steps say to enable TurboMCP in the project, build and open the editor. They do not say that each user must also tick Enable TurboMCP in Editor Preferences and restart. The README quick start has the same gap. A user who follows the steps gets an editor with no TurboMCP tools, panel or hooks.
  4. When TurboMCP is off, the status tool is also absent, as the guide says. An agent that cannot find any TurboMCP tool cannot ask TurboMCP why. The guide points to Editor Preferences and the startup log message, but the install steps do not.
records.reported_title: The installation guide says Enable TurboMCP defaults to enabled, but the code defaults it to off (medium)
records.implementation: README, installation and troubleshooting now match default OFF, existing saved preferences, per-user opt-in, restart and unavailable disabled status tool. Compared with Settings.h and Module.cpp; no settings or runtime changes.

records.title: Investigate engine writer corruption and design safe data-asset edits
records.observation: The writer refused every key ("is not a subobject of the property owner") and reported that the property could not be set. A read-back then showed the map reduced to one entry with a None key. The asset was dirty in memory.
records.reported_title: Engine object writer replaced a whole map in memory while reporting failure (high)
records.implementation: Stock bypass-map corruption reproduced and retained as an external engine defect/proposal. Safe plugin read/preview/edit tools now validate temporary values, target exact entries/owned children, require Unicode-safe revisions, verify actual results and report complete or failed restoration honestly. Native workflow covers real InputAction settings, map identities, preview, refusal, no-op, undo, callback mismatch, failed restoration and live help. Historical X-116 input formats remain unknown; no claim that the stock engine was repaired. See docs/audit/data-asset-tool-review.json for scope and limitations.
records.implementation_limits: Bounded workflow acceptance; see task review for retained failures, unsupported cases and external engine limitations.
